back: The income from sales: price × quantity sold.
TR ÷ quantity sold; equal to the price when all units sell at one price.
The change in TR from selling one more unit: ΔTR ÷ ΔQ.
Price = AR = MR at every output; TR rises in a straight line from the origin.

front: Why is MR below price when a firm must cut its price to sell more?
back: The lower price applies to all units, so revenue is lost on the earlier units.

front: What happens to total revenue when price falls and demand is elastic?
back: TR rises: the percentage rise in sales is bigger than the percentage fall in price.

front: What happens to total revenue when price rises and demand is inelastic?
back: TR rises: sales fall by a smaller percentage than the price rises.
Revenue is income from sales; profit = total revenue − total cost.
More sales at the same price raise TR; advertising, quality, new markets and rising incomes can raise sales.
